target_customer: AI, analytics, CI and serverless teams that run workloads over large S3 datasets
problem: Workloads need fast POSIX file access to data in S3 without copying it; Archil exposes buckets as a fast, shared, unlimited disk and now sells sandboxes and durable disks for agents.
business_model: Usage-based cloud storage and compute infrastructure
product_category: Cloud file system and agent runtime, developer infrastructure

founders.name: Hunter Leath
prior_employers: Amazon Web Services (founding engineer then senior product manager on Elastic File System)
founders.background_notes: About nine years in cloud storage per the YC page and the Felicis post; education not found.

competitors.name: Mountpoint for Amazon S3
competitors.what: AWS file client for mounting S3 buckets with limited POSIX support
competitors.traction_then: Existing AWS tool; limitations include no file locks, random writes or renames per Archil's docs

competitors.name: s3fs-fuse
competitors.what: Older open source FUSE mount of S3 with broad POSIX subset, reported unstable under parallel load

technical_complexity.rationale: A POSIX compatible, shared, cached file system on object storage with consistency and write back is distributed systems work that few teams can do; the founder built EFS at AWS.

defensibility.rationale: Hard engineering and data gravity help, but AWS can ship its own: Amazon S3 Files was introduced in April 2026.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AWS introduced Amazon S3 Files in April 2026, a managed way to mount a bucket as a file system, directly overlapping the original wedge; Archil moved toward sandboxes and disks for agents.

market_need_then: AI and analytics workloads store large datasets in S3 but need file semantics and speed; the pain was long standing (the company calls it a 20 year problem) and boosted by AI training and agents.

identity.visual_style: Developer infrastructure site with a data layer cable illustration
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, 'The serverless runtime for intelligence', 'Run here. Work from anywhere.'

rebrands.why: The founder said the new name better reflects help with data management beyond pure storage.

brand_strength.rationale: Developer brand with Hacker News launches and a podcast appearance but no distinctive brand assets found.

pivots.from: Regatta Storage, an S3 backed POSIX file system
pivots.to: Archil, a data company then an agent runtime with sandboxes and durable disks
pivots.why: Company said it wanted to go beyond pure storage; the sandbox positioning appears later and is undated.

outcome_analysis: Archil, formerly Regatta Storage, raised a 6.7 million dollar seed led by Felicis in June 2025 and cites customers such as Clay, Gamma and Depot. A Series A of 11 million dollars is reported only on aggregators. The founder's EFS experience is a strong fit, though AWS shipped S3 Files in April 2026, pushing Archil toward agent infrastructure.
notes: FundUp lists an 11 million Series A dated 2026-04-20 and Standout lists 18.0 million total; neither confirmed by a press release or the company, so no Series A recorded. Competitor sources are undated documentation pages, so source_date is null; these tools existed at the Nov 2024 launch but the sources do not date their state. Name origin not found. The YC page lists a team of 11 but only one founder.
